title: Sell Mineral Rights in Harrisville, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Harrisville, WV | Ritchie County Seat
metaDescription: Harrisville, WV is Ritchie County's seat and its oldest oil-lease record. We buy legacy and Marcellus-era mineral interests here directly, no obligation.
heroLead: Harrisville is the Ritchie County seat, home to the courthouse that holds the deed and lease record for one of the oldest oil-producing counties in the country.
intro: Ritchie County's oil history goes back to the earliest days of American petroleum production, and Harrisville's Clerk's office holds instruments reflecting that: shallow Big Injun and Gordon sand leases from the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, still on the books, sitting underneath modern Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant leases signed within the last fifteen years.

We buy oil and gas mineral and royalty interests in and around Harrisville directly, and because the county courthouse record here runs so deep, we do the work of reading every layer of a tract's lease history before making an offer.

sections.heading: A courthouse record older than most in the state
paragraphs: As the county seat, Harrisville's deed books document conveyances and leases going back further than in many surrounding communities. That depth is useful for verification, but it also means Harrisville-area tracts frequently carry more layered ownership history to untangle.

sections.heading: Shallow wells and deep units on the same ground
paragraphs: It's routine here to find a legacy shallow well, sometimes still nominally producing, on the same tract as a modern Marcellus or Utica unit. Each pays under separate terms, and we evaluate both rather than assuming one lease governs everything.

sections.heading: Flat-rate leases from the earliest era
paragraphs: Some of Ritchie County's oldest leases predate West Virginia's statutory minimum one-eighth royalty for flat-rate leases. We check whether a Harrisville-area lease qualifies for conversion before pricing the interest.

sections.heading: Generations of heirs on century-old tracts
paragraphs: Tracts with this much history have typically split across many generations. We regularly work with Harrisville-area interests held by ten or more heirs and buy individual shares without requiring the family to agree collectively.

faqs.question: How far back does the Harrisville lease record go?
faqs.answer: Some Ritchie County instruments date to the earliest era of American oil production. We can trace and evaluate leases this old.

faqs.question: Can I have separate royalty from a legacy well and a modern Marcellus unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, if both cover your tract and are active, each pays under its own lease or unit order.

faqs.question: Is my family's old lease a flat-rate lease?
faqs.answer: Check the recorded language, a fixed dollar figure per well indicates a flat-rate lease, which may be eligible for statutory conversion. We verify this for you.
